telegram: 🔑 Your rule binds the key, not the wallet We tested it on Tau Net testnet today. A fresh test account wrote itself one rule: nothing above 1,000 AGRS leaves (block 165). Then the same key signed a payment of 5,000, this time with IDNI's own command-line wallet, not with tauhud.com. The node refused it: "the sender's own policy clause blocked transfer #1". A payment of 500 went through (block 166). Why it matters: the rule lives on the chain, not in an app. Every node checks every payment against the sender's own rule, when it takes it in and again when it reads the block, whatever program signed it. Honest limit: whoever holds the key can also change the rule. It stops a mistaken or pressured payment, not a stolen key. Write your own rule: https://tauhud.com/wallet/#rules-mine

In most wallets, a spending limit is just an app setting. Sign with another app and it's gone.

On Tau Net, the limit lives on the chain.

Today on the testnet an account set "nothing above 1,000 leaves". The same key signed 5,000 in another wallet. The node said no.
